profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary: For over a decade, I've been helping architects use technology to enhance their practice. I do my best to keep up with new developments in 3D technology, which are in no short supply these days. I've also got a background in programming, and try to keep my skills sharp with personal projects as often as I can. If you play Wordle, I may have a project you'll find interesting...

positions.title: 3D Production Manager
positions.description: As 3D production manager, I was responsible for the firm's effective use of 3D technology. I designed and improved 3D production workflows, set and enforced 3D CAD standards, trained staff, screened new hires, collected performance data on the firm's 3D activities, and assisted the managing partners in strategic decision making around 3D. In addition to my administrative duties, I was also the firm's primary 3D renderer. I produced digital models that capture design intent, and used them to create compelling images that drove client approval. It was up to me to make sure our rendering work was high-quality, and delivered on time.

positions.title: Rapid Prototyping specialist
positions.description: I held primary responsibility for the production of accurate, highly detailed architectural models using an Objet 3D printer. I was also responsible for keeping the model making work flow up to date, and made significant changes over the years in order to improve speed, reliability, and the level of detail we can achieve.

positions.title: Summer GIS Intern (2007)
positions.description: In my second summer with the MTA, my work focused more on map making and statistical analysis.  I was tasked with designing, developing, and implementing an exploratory analysis for relatively new data.  Primary goals were to discern whether a more long-term approach to studying the locations of collisions on the various facilities would be worthwhile, and looking for any correlation between collision occurrence and summons issuing.  I also continued to produce maps with a more narrow scope as needed.

positions.title: Residential Life Intern
positions.description: Hampshire College does not have a real equivaltent to the tradional RA.  The closest position they have is that of an Intern.  A chief difference is that Interns are not a disciplinary force by any means.  While we were expected to make sure students were aware of the community norms, we had no particular ability to enforce those rules.  Our primary tasks were those of conflict resolution and advocacy, offering mediation between students, and acting as an intermediary between students and professional housing staff.  As Interns are the first line of defense in terms of maintaining a generally peaceful campus, the selection process is quite rigorous, and the positions are reserved for students who demonstrate particular coolheadedness, responsibility, and courtesy.

positions.title: Summer GIS Intern (2006)
positions.description: In my first summer with the MTA, my primary job was to design, develop, test, and deploy a number of Python scripts, in order to automate a number of rather tedious data conversion tasks.  The MTA has many CAD files they need to add to their GIS database, and a very specific manner in which they need this process to be done.  If done manually, this process takes about fifteen minutes per file, and with the staggering number of files they need to transfer, this easily translates to multiple years of work devoted soley to data conversion.  The script I developed not only saved time by automating this conversion, but it also allowed the user to check the files' adherence to various quality standards, and automatically enforced a given organizational scheme.  Additionally, as the script could run in the background, the user could work on other, more pressing, tasks while the conversion was underway.
